articles.title: Global Market: Indonesia stock exchange to meet MSCI after downgrade warning triggers market rout
articles.content: Indonesia’s stock exchange will meet MSCI on Monday to seek clarity over a warning that could strip the country of its emerging-market status. The threat triggered a sharp selloff, wiping $65 billion off market capitalisation on Friday. A downgrade could prompt foreign fund outflows and weaken investor participation in Indonesian equities.

articles.title: HFCL Q2 Results: Profit zooms 448% YoY to Rs 394 crore; stock hits 5% upper circuit
articles.content: HFCL reported a 448% year-on-year jump in Q2FY27 net profit to Rs 394 crore, compared with Rs 71.92 crore a year ago. Revenue surged 144% to Rs 2,542 crore, while EBITDA rose 224% to Rs 658 crore. EBITDA margin expanded 640 basis points to 25.89%. The optical fibre and AI beneficiary’s stock hit the 5% upper circuit at Rs 268.70 on the BSE and has gained nearly 300% so far this year.

articles.title: India bonds rise after flat open as sharp drop in US yields spurs value buying
articles.content: The Indian government bond market saw a positive turnaround as US Treasury yields declined, prompting significant value purchases. The benchmark 6.94% bond maturing in 2036 observed a yield of 7.3551% in morning trading. Concurrently, oil prices dipped, fueled by expectations of improved supply following lifted sanctions on Russia. With India's consumer inflation rising to 5.54%, the Reserve Bank of India may respond with tighter financial conditions amidst ongoing capital outflows.

articles.title: Sugar stocks Balrampur Chini, Bajaj Sugar, others crash up to 7% as centre stops diversion to ethanol
articles.content: Sugar stocks dropped in early trading following the government's directive to cease sugar diversion for ethanol production. The decision impacts major sugar companies like Balrampur Chini Mills and Bajaj Hindusthan Sugar, which experienced a decline between 2% and 7%. This directive aims to enhance domestic sugar availability amidst rising prices. The government's action follows concerns about potential production shortfalls due to insufficient rainfall.
